name: Citizenship by Marriage

requirements.blocker_text: Requires lawful residence in Montenegro for at least 5 years, of which at least 3 years must be married to a Montenegrin citizen, with the wedding having taken place in Montenegro, and no single absence from the country longer than 30 days during that period. Applied without gender distinction between spouses.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years' lawful residence including 3 years of marriage to a Montenegrin citizen, with the wedding held in Montenegro.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' lawful residence with no 30+ day absences

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 5 years' lawful residence, no single absence over 30 days

sources.title: Lawyers Montenegro (private legal-guide site) -- marriage-based citizenship: 5 years' lawful residence with at least 3 years of marriage to a Montenegrin citizen, wedding held in Montenegro, no absence exceeding 30 days, applied without gender distinction

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Montenegro). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a private legal-guide site (tier 3), same limitation as me_citizenship_by_descent.json. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING, WORTH FLAGGING AGAINST THE PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY THIS SESSION: unlike Iran, Lebanon, Tunisia, Pakistan, Somalia, Ghana, Tanzania, and Senegal's marriage-citizenship routes elsewhere in this dataset -- all of which favor a foreign wife over a foreign husband -- Montenegro's provision, as described in the source reviewed, applies without gender distinction to either spouse. It is a genuinely demanding route in absolute terms though: 5 years' residence (not merely 3 years of marriage) with strict absence limits and a requirement that the wedding itself took place in Montenegro, is a specific and unusually precise condition set not seen in quite this form elsewhere in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set false per the same general non-acceptance noted in me_citizenship_by_descent.json and me_citizenship_naturalisation.json.
